item.title: Token Logit Biasing Moves from Theory to Production Encoders
item.description: By subtly shifting token sampling distributions at generation time, text watermarking bakes origin keys directly into output sequences—trading marginal model entropy for a hard provenance signal. The risk lies in fragile compliance: simple paraphrasing and local re-encoding can still wash away the mark while degrading genuine engineering oversight into passive signal-checking.

item.title: Scaling Laws Meet Silicon Limits: Why Theoretical FLOPs Break Down in the Datacenter
item.description: Chinchilla-style compute-optimal scaling equations assume frictionless hardware, but real-world cluster topologies introduce communication overhead and memory bandwidth bounds that stall real-world execution. Optimizing strictly for theoretical FLOP efficiency risks idling multi-million dollar GPU clusters, forcing engineers to trade mathematical perfection for physical throughput.
